correctness.rationale: For exactly seven binary points, affine relation vectors have even weights in {4,6}; disjoint radius-one spheres in the odd parity class give relation dimension at most 3. Dimensions 0,1,2 have exactly 1,2,2 types; dimension 3 has uniquely the simplex code by the weight-sum and character-inversion argument. Quotient constructions realize all six, while the MacWilliams identity computes all four magnitude probabilities and distinguishes the six affine orbits. The proof covers arbitrary d>=3. An independent direct-character checker verified every eligible relation subspace (1+42+175+30=248) and all 11440 seven-subsets of F2^4; this corroboration is not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: Because seven is odd, Fourier support and convolution rank are completely uninformative for distinguishing seven-point binary indicators. The complete four-level magnitude distribution nevertheless reconstructs the full affine class in every dimension, a natural finite harmonic inverse invariant. All six profiles and their precise affine geometries are classified, including the unique Fano/simplex case, and five nontrivial alternatives. This addresses a coherent inverse problem, not an arbitrary table or a mere zero-free parity deduction; it complements the established adjacent six- and eight-point studies. Claims of noise stability or general support sizes are not made.
